claim: A meta-analysis of 15 comparative cohort studies (3873 patients) found pooled seizure freedom of 52.5% after LITT vs 67.1% after open resective surgery (RR 0.78, 95% CI 0.70-0.88), but no significant difference in propensity-score-matched studies (RR 0.85) or TLE studies (RR 0.88); LITT had fewer complications.

bibliographic_record.authors: Pichardo-Rojas D, Espinosa-Cantú CB, Valenzuela-Rangel AF, et al.
bibliographic_record.title: A comparative assessment of laser interstitial thermal therapy and open resective surgery for drug-resistant epilepsy: a meta-analysis of 3873 patients

supporting_passage: LITT showed a significantly lower rate of SF compared to ORS (risk ratio [RR] 0.78, 95% CI 0.70-0.88, p ≤ 0.0001). However, when PSM studies (RR 0.85, 95% CI 0.63-1.15, p = 0.30) and studies on patients with temporal lobe epilepsy (TLE) (RR 0.88, 95% CI 0.67-1.14, p = 0.34) were analyzed, the SF rates were similar.
passage_location: Abstract, Results section. Abstract only (full text not read). Europe PMC REST API (resultType=core, abstractText) for PMID 40911916; https://europepmc.org/abstract/MED/40911916; accessed 2026-11-01

population_and_design.design: meta-analysis of 15 comparative cohort studies (no RCTs); search to 2024-03-14
population_and_design.population: focal drug-resistant epilepsy, mixed ages and etiologies (subgroups by age, etiology, PSM)

endpoint.reported_endpoint: seizure freedom (definition and follow-up not_reported in abstract)

reported_observation: Unmatched: open surgery higher SF; matched and TLE subgroups: no significant difference; LITT shorter stay and fewer complications.
author_inference: Across unmatched studies ORS showed higher SF, but matched analyses showed no difference; prospective matched studies needed.
contradictions: Ekman 2024 reports TLR superior to LITT in mesial TLE (72.5% vs 57.1%, P<0.01), whereas this paper's TLE subgroup shows no significant difference (RR 0.88, p=0.34).
overlap_note: Pools comparative cohorts likely overlapping with Maroufi 2026 and Ekman 2024; not independent evidence.
